title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: k is a commutative base ring. For a k-module M, V(M) = Spec Sym_k(M) is the 'linear scheme' (EGA II 1.7). As a functor on k-algebras it is A ↦ Hom_k(M, A).

On the previous page, a morphism of k-schemes u*: V(N) → V(M) was identified with a k-linear map u: M → Sym N, decomposed as u = Σ_i u_i with u_i: M → Sym^i N. Composing with the homothety λ on V(N) corresponds to u ↦ u^λ = Σ λ^i u_i. Homogeneity of degree n means u*∘λ_{V(N)} = λ^n_{V(M)}∘u* for all A and λ ∈ A. Taking A = k[T], λ = T gives Σ(T^i − T^n) u_i(x) = 0 in Sym N[T]. Comparing coefficients gives u_i(x) = 0 for i ≠ n. Since x is arbitrary, u_i = 0 for i ≠ n, i.e. u factors through Sym^n N.

This page draws the conclusions.
(1) Morphisms V(N) → V(M) that are homogeneous of degree 1 correspond exactly to k-linear maps M → N. These are automatically linear for the ring scheme O_k = G_a, i.e. additive and not just compatible with homotheties. Hence the contravariant functor M ↦ V(M), from k-modules to k-schemes with G_a-action (or to O_k-module functors), is fully faithful.
(2) The same method describes morphisms from a product ∏_{α∈I} V(N_α) → F. One uses the evident isomorphism ∏ V(N_α) ≅ V(⊕ N_α), a special case of the remark that V sends arbitrary colimits of modules to limits: Hom_k(colim N, A) = lim Hom_k(N_i, A).
(3) For F = V(M), a morphism ∏ V(N_α) → V(M) is a linear map u: M → Sym(⊕N_α) = ⊗_α Sym(N_α), the latter a restricted tensor product. It decomposes by multidegree i = (i_α) ∈ N^(I) as u = Σ u_(i), with u_(i): M → ⊗_α Sym^{i_α} N_α.

The next page completes the argument. Multihomogeneity of multidegree n_ means u lands in ⊗ Sym^{n_α} N_α. Multilinear pairings ∏ V(N_α) → V(M) therefore correspond to M → ⊗ N_α; in particular bilinear pairings V(N) × V(N') → V(M) correspond to M → N ⊗ N'.

Purpose: this is foundational bookkeeping for the divided-power de Rham complex lectures (IHÉS 1976). It identifies linear and multilinear structures on vector-group schemes with module data, presumably so that Sym/Γ, products and pairings can be handled functorially.
errors: The displayed identity Sym^i(⊕N_α) = ⊗_α Sym^i(N_α) is wrong if read literally with a single integer i. The correct statements are Sym(⊕N_α) ≅ ⊗_α Sym(N_α) (restricted tensor product when I is infinite) and Sym^n(⊕N_α) ≅ ⊕_{|i|=n} ⊗_α Sym^{i_α}(N_α). The next line, which decomposes by multidegree i = (i_α), shows Grothendieck intends the multi-index version.
'décomposer M suivant les multidegrés' should be 'décomposer u': it is the map u (equivalently the target algebra) that is graded by multidegree, not M.
For infinite I, multidegrees must have finite support (N^(I) rather than N^I). The 'multidegree (1,1,...)' case leading to ⊗_α N_α on the next page only makes sense for finite I.
'(comme n arbitraire)' should logically be '(comme x arbitraire)': the vanishing of u_i(x) for each x gives u_i = 0. This is a slip either in the handwriting or in the transcription.

ideas.what: Morphisms V(N) → V(M) homogeneous of degree n correspond to linear maps M → Sym^n N; degree-1 morphisms are linear maps M → N, giving full faithfulness of M ↦ V(M)
ideas.modern_name: Linear schemes / vector group schemes associated to a module; homogeneous polynomial maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (EGA II §1.7; SGA 3 Exp. I, Demazure–Grothendieck)
ideas.where_published: EGA II 1.7; SGA 3 Exposé I (functors W(E), V(E))

ideas.what: V turns arbitrary colimits of modules into limits; ∏V(N_α) ≅ V(⊕N_α)
ideas.modern_name: Representable functor Hom(-, A) sends colimits to limits

ideas.what: Multihomogeneous morphisms ∏V(N_α) → V(M) of multidegree n correspond to M → ⊗ Sym^{n_α}N_α; multilinear pairings correspond to M → ⊗N_α
ideas.modern_name: Multihomogeneous polynomial maps / multilinear maps of vector group schemes (dual form of Roby's polynomial laws)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine foundational verification of standard facts about V(M) = Spec Sym M (homogeneity, full faithfulness, products and multilinear pairings), already in EGA II and SGA 3. It only serves as background for the divided-power de Rham lectures.
transcription_corrections: '(comme n arbitraire)' is likely '(comme x arbitraire)' given the logic; the handwriting is ambiguous.
'O_h-linéaires' is probably 'O_k-linéaires', i.e. linear for the ring scheme O_k = G_a over k.
The crossed-out expression below ∏V(N_i) → F reads V(∐_i N_i), struck through, consistent with the transcription.
